newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Lauritzen sees delayed shipyard payment.
newsitem.headline: Danish Lauritzen sees delayed shipyard payment.

text.p: Danish shipping and shipbuilding group J.Lauritzen said on Thursday that payment for the sale of a 48 percent stake in its Danyard unit to a Malaysian buyer could be delayed beyond its August target.

"We have no control over when the (Malaysian) government will approve the deal, but it could well take a little longer than we originally thought," Lauritzen managing director Bent Oestergaard told Reuters.
He declined to give further details.

On April 1, Lauritzen finalised the sale of 48 percent of its Danyard shipbuilding unit to the Penang Shipbuilding Construction (PSC) group, with the deal subject to the approval of the Malaysian authorities.
PSC at that time paid a one million dollar deposit.
Lauritzen had expected the $100 million deal would be approved by July, whereupon PSC would pay a further $9.0 million, and payment would be completed in August.

According to a letter of intent signed last December the final purchase sum could be revised depending on the result of an independent evaluation of Danyard by British consultants Jones Lang & Wootton but Oestergaard said Lauritzen had not yet seen the report.
"We are in contact with PSC and expect to see the report," Oestergaard said. --Stig Oerskov Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969659
